recipes.name: Red, White, and Blue-Misu
ingredients_raw: 1 (9 inch) angel food cake, cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Beat cream in a large bowl until stiff peaks form; gently fold in mascarpone until well incorporated. Set aside.
Place ½ strawberries in a blender; blend until smooth. Transfer puréed strawberries to a large bowl; stir in remaining whole strawberries and blueberries.

Layer ⅓ angel food cake cubes in bottom of a trifle or serving bowl. Cover with ⅓ berry mixture; gently spoon ⅓ whipped cream mixture over berries. Repeat layers twice more, ending with cream mixture. Chill until ready to serve.
Shave chocolate using a vegetable peeler, letting curls fall on top of dessert.

raw_recipe.headline: Red, White, and Blue-Misu
raw_recipe.description: Inspired by Italian tiramisu and British trifle, this red, white, and blue-misu recipe layers whipped mascarpone and cream, angel food cake, and berries.

review.reviewBody: see my notes--use fresh berries, make natural sauce by adding sugar [not much} a squeeze of lemon juice and a little grand marnier. Cream- add sugar, sugar vanilla and grand marnier!
Everyone enjoyed this recipe and it seemed to be a hit. Next time I think I'll try fresh fruit instead of frozen. Although it was good with the frozen and still not too sweet.

I made this with fresh berries and I should have read the hints to add sugar and vanilla, as we found it a bit bland, especially the cheese/cream mixture. I will make again using the suggestions in the reviews.

This is an excellent recipe as others have said. However, I agree with other reviewers that it requires a couple of tweaks to make it truly outstanding. First of all, you really should use fresh fruit, not frozen. Also, you need sugar and some type of flavoring both for the berry mixture and the cream mixture. Otherwise, it really is quite bland. I found Grand Marnier was the perfect flavor to complement the berries, much better than coffee liqueur would be. With those changes, it was a hit both times I've made it so far. And it's beautiful to look at too, bonus!
Looks good! I LOVE LOVE LOVE your title! Adorable! Love this recipe and all I'm doing is looking at it all day! THANK YOU SO MUCH!!!!
This received rave reviews at my brother's annual July 4 weekend cookout! Everyone wanted the recipe. Next time I'm going to try it with peaches and raspberries!
I made this for a 4th of July party and it was a huge hit!! I liked that it wasn't too sweet! My new fave!

Very pretty presentation, but really lacked in flavor. The cream/cheese mixture does need some added flavor, whether it be some sugar or vanilla. We had to mix the whole thing together because the cream just overpowered everything else. Will try it again sometime with some adjustments to the cream layer.
Made for the 4th and my guests LOVED this dessert! I added a pinch of sugar and vanilla to the cream mixture and it was wonderful!
This is a very refreshing twist to a classic tiramisu. I could only give it four stars because it does lack a little in flavor without the coffee liquer. I will definatly make this again.
